About the School
We are a high-performing, inclusive secondary school at the heart of the East Reading community. Our urban setting brings a rich diversity and vibrancy, reflecting the multicultural community we serve. Our scale allows us to know our students well and foster a strong sense of connection. Relationships are purposeful and consistent, helping every student develop their skills, talents and sense of purpose.
Our values — Aim High, Be Inclusive, Work Together — shape every part of school life. From academic challenge to creative expression and team sport, students are encouraged to participate fully and pursue their ambitions with confidence. We see our school as a place where energy and commitment to excellence go hand in hand — where the corridors are busy, ideas are shared, and young people develop the character and skills they need to flourish.
Having worked in schools for more than 20 years, including in senior leadership across a range of contexts, I am passionate about the power of education to transform lives. What I value most about Maiden Erlegh School in Reading is the aspiration and pride of our students, the commitment of our staff, and the partnerships we build with families and our wider community.
I warmly invite you to visit us. We would be delighted to welcome you and show you what makes our school such a distinctive and ambitious place to learn and grow.
Mrs Sarah Gibbs, Headteacher

Careers, Work Experience and Work Related Learning
Careers, Work Experience and Work Related Learning
Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance (CEIAG) at Maiden Erlegh School in Reading is seen as an important part of school life and all students will receive this as part of their learning here at the school. We are committed to providing the appropriate activities and experiences to enable students to make successful transitions from Foundation Stage to Key Stage 4 and further education, training programmes, apprenticeships or work.
Our school's careers programme embed equality and diversity considerations throughout.
Maiden Erlegh School in Reading aims in relation to CEIAG are:
Careers education at Maiden Erlegh School in Reading should not just be seen as learning about jobs but also learning about work ethics, equipping students with skills (both hard and soft) for the work place, ensuring transition occurs smoothly and helping to reduce barriers to entering the world of work.
In this section you will find lots of useful links and information about careers, services, further education and training programmes including: information on careers fairs, volunteering, work experience etc.
If you wish to discuss the careers programme further, please contact our school Lead for Careers and Destinations, Mr D Hood.
(d.hood@maidenerleghtrust.org).
Please see our Key Policies page here and scroll down for the Provider Access Policy.

Personal Development
Personal Development
At Maiden Erlegh School in Reading we recognise the personal development of students is a fundamental part of our academic and pastoral work. It is our intention to create good local, national and global citizens, who develop good character and resilience. To this end, we aim to develop students spiritually, morally, socially and culturally and ensure that they are treated as individuals whilst doing this. We aim to teach students about British values, mutual respect and tolerance.
We aim to deliver spiritual, moral, social and cultural education through all aspects of school life; curriculum, extra-curricular activities, the pastoral system, assemblies as well as themed events.
Our personal development provision incorporates recommendations laid out by the Department for Education and the PSHE Association.
Topics for all students are grouped into 7 core themes:
Aside from Sex Education (which is predominately delivered with by the RE team in Key Stage 3 and 4), these sessions will be delivered by teachers as part of our school curriculum and will be relevant to the age, understanding, cultural background and circumstances of the students. They will also reflect their needs in terms of language, learning styles and abilities.

Maiden Erlegh School in Reading is an inclusive school. We welcome all students and look to assist students to overcome all barriers to learning.
Our priority for children with special educational needs is to provide high quality teaching and pastoral care and effective interventions.
Our SENCO is Mrs N Benham, contacted via the school office – main email address.
In all of this work we aim to work as closely as possible with parents and carers to complement the work they do in supporting their child towards these goals.

Enrichment Curriculum
Maiden Erlegh School in Reading is proud to be able to offer a wide and varied selection of enrichment learning for our students outside of the core curriculum. Enrichment activities are organised by the Curriculum Departments. These include a full range of sporting, cultural and artistic activities; delivered during regular clubs and activities related to specific subjects. In addition, trips and visits during the school day, in the evening and over longer periods involving overnight stays all serve to add value to the taught curriculum. The enrichment programme offered at Maiden Erlegh School in Reading is available to all students from Year 7 through to Year 11, with the aim of creating a holistic student that has qualities and skills both in and out of the classroom.
